jogavel, use assets leves pra que rode sem travar no navegador,
use as skills de design disponiveis e se necessario vasculhe a internet para apoio.

tool_input.content:
# SPEC — DOOM Clone (Three.js) · Contrato de Entrega

> Gran-Mestre · 2026-08-13 · Rota: COMPLEX · Versão 1.0

## 1. Objetivo

Jogo FPS completo estilo **DOOM (1993)** construído com **Three.js**, 100% procedural
(sem assets binários externos — texturas e sons gerados em runtime), leve o suficiente
para rodar fluido (~60 FPS) no navegador em hardware comum.

## 2. Requisitos Funcionais (do pedido do usuário)

| # | Requisito | Detalhe |
|---|-----------|---------|
| R1 | Tech stack | Three.js + JS (ES Modules) + HTML5 + CSS. Sem build step pesado (pode usar módulos ES nativos + import map). |
| R2 | Armas | **Pelo menos 4**: Pistola (hitscan), Shotgun (spread hitscan), Chaingun (full-auto hitscan), Rocket Launcher (projétil + splash). Alternância por roda do mouse / teclas 1-4. Munição e recuo por arma. |
| R3 | Inimigos | **Pelo menos 3**: (a) Zumbi/Former Human — hitscan fraco; (b) Imp — projétil de plasma; (c) Demon/Pinky — corpo-a-corpo veloz; bônus (d) Barão de Hell — mini-chefão tanque. IA: idle/chase/attack/morte. |
| R4 | Física detalhada | Aceleração/atrito no movimento, strafe, run; gravidade + pulo; colisão AABB por célula do grid (raycast DDA para hitscan e visão); colisão com inimigos (empurrar); splash damage com falloff por raio; view bobbing; portas animadas; projéteis sem gravidade com colisão contra grid e entidades. |
| R5 | Minimap | Overlay canvas 2D (canto) com mapa, paredes, posição do jogador, direção de visão, inimigos vistos/ativos. |
| R6 | HUD | Health, munição por arma, arma ativa, crosshair, dano recebido (flash), morte, mensagens de pickup, tela inicial + tela de vitória. |
| R7 | Itens | Health packs, ammo, armor — com bob e pickup. |
| R8 | Áudio | WebAudio **sintetizado** (tiros, hits, explosões, dano, pickup, morte, ambiência) — zero arquivos. |
| R9 | Assets leves | Tudo procedural: texturas via canvas, geometria low-poly, InstancedMesh para inimigos/projéteis, sem sombras caras, pixel ratio limitado, texturas pequenas (≤256px). Zero dependência externa além do three.module.js local (baixado para o projeto). |
| R10 | Jogável | Pointer Lock, mouse para olhar, correção de porte, dificuldade balanceada, vitória ao zerar o mapa (matar todos / alcançar saída). |
| R11 | Design | UI/HUD com qualidade de design (skill /shared/frontend) — estética militar-retrô coesa, tipografia legível, estados visuais claros. |
| R12 | Validação | Testes unitários (node, lógica pura separada da Three) + **QA real com Playwright**: abrir, navegar, atirar, matar inimigos, coletar itens, screenshot, FPS. |

## 3. Arquitetura (fisicamente separada: lógica pura ↔ render)

```
index.html            — shell + import map (three local)
css/style.css         — HUD, telas, minimap container, design system
js/constants.js       — ⚙️ puro: mapas, física, armas, inimigos, itens (tabelas de dados)
js/map.js             — ⚙️ puro: grid, parse, raycast DDA, linha de visão, portas (estado)
js/player-physics.js  — ⚙️ puro: movimento, colisão AABB, gravidade, pulo
js/weapons-core.js    — ⚙️ puro: dano, splash falloff, ammo, recuo (math)
js/engine.js          — 🎨 Three.js: renderer, cena, luzes, loop, instancing
js/level.js           — 🎨 constrói geometria do nível a partir do grid puro
js/player.js          — 🎨 câmera, input, aplica física, viewmodel
js/weapons.js         — 🎨 viewmodels (malhas procedurais), hitscan visual, projéteis
js/enemies.js         — 🎨 meshes de inimigos + IA (consome dados puros)
js/minimap.js         — 🎨 canvas 2D overlay
js/hud.js             — 🎨 DOM/CSS: barras, números, crosshair, telas
js/audio.js           — 🎨 WebAudio sintetizado
js/particles.js       — 🎨 sistema de partículas pool
js/main.js            — bootstrap + state machine (menu/playing/gameover/win)
tests/map.test.mjs        — grid + DDA + visão
tests/physics.test.mjs    — colisão/movimento
tests/weapons.test.mjs    — dano/splash/ammo
tests/level.test.mjs      — parse/render-data
```

⚠️ Arquivos marcados ⚙️ **não importam Three.js** (100% testáveis em node). 🎨 importam.

## 4. Física — especificação detalhada

| Parâmetro | Valor | Notas |
|-----------|-------|-------|
| Escala | 1 unidade ≈ 1 metro | Grid: célula de 1 u |
| Player radius | 0.40 u | AABB cilíndrica para colisão |
| Player altura | 1.80 u | eye height 1.62 u |
| Walk speed | 4.2 u/s | |
| Run (Shift) | 6.2 u/s | |
| Aceleração | ~1.4 s até topo | exponencial suave, Doom-feel |
| Atrito | decai ~4x/s | |
| Gravidade | 28 u/s² | |
| Jump velocity | 9.5 u/s | ≈ 1.6 u de altura |
| Colisão | swept por eixo (X e Z separados) | sliding contra paredes |
| Colisão inimigos | push suave (player mais pesado) | entraves de passagem |
| Hitscan range | 800 u | DDA contra grid + AABB inimigos |
| Splash | raio 6 u, falloff linear | auto-dano ativo |
| Projéteis | 6–14 u/s sem gravidade | rocket 10 u/s |
| Portas | animação 1.2 s, colidível | ativadas por proximidade/interação |
| View bob | seno 0.02 u @ step frequency | + recuo por arma |

## 5. Armas (DPS balanceado)

| Arma | Dano | Cadência | Spread | Munição | Notas |
|------|------|----------|--------|---------|-------|
| Pistola | 5–10 (7 pelotas=1) | 2.5/s | 0° | Infinita → balas | precisa, zoom leve |
| Shotgun | 7×0.5 (5 pelotas) | 0.9/s | ±4° | Balas 8/peca | alto burst |
| Chaingun | 4–7 | 9/s | ±2° | Balas | full-auto |
| Rocket | 60–90 (+splash) | 0.55/s | 0° | Foguetes | auto-dano, área |

## 6. Inimigos

| Nome | HP | Dano | Velocidade | Tipo | Recompensa |
|------|----|------|------------|------|-----------|
| Zumbi | 20 | 3–8 | 2.0 | hitscan 8/s | balas |
| Imp | 60 | 8–16 | 3.0 | projétil 3 u/s | balas |
| Demon (Pinky) | 150 | 10–20 | 4.5 | melee | balas |
| Barão | 400 | 15–24 | 2.2 | projétil duplo | health/armor |

IA: estados `IDLE(0) → CHASE → ATTACK`; visão por cone 60° + linha-de-visão DDA;
distância de aggro 14 u; mantém distância ótima por arma; morte → partículas + drop.

## 7. Mapa

Grid textual 24×24 com legendas: `#` parede, `.` chão, `P` spawn player,
`Z/I/D/B` spawns inimigos, `H/A/M` itens (health/armor/ammo), `E` porta, `>` saída.
Layout: arena principal + corredores + sala chefe. Texturas procedurais:
startan (vermelho), tech (cinza), brick, emblema (logo). Teto/chão com variação.

## 8. Qualidade & Critérios de Trânsito (R28)

- Testes unitários node P/GGEM → `PASSOU_CATEGORICO` (todos verdes).
- QA Playwright real (R29): jogo abre, pointer lock, dispara, HUD atualiza,
  inimigo morre, dano funciona, minimap renderiza, FPS ≥ 30 em screenshot.
- Verificação visual (R30): screenshots avaliados — estética coerente, sem
  artefatos, HUD legível.
- Arquivos ≤ 400 linhas, funções ≤ 50 linhas, sem console.log, zero segredos.

## 9. Não-escopo (v1)

- Sem multiplayer, sem save/load, sem sistema de níveis múltiplos (1 mapa master),

# SPEC — DOOM Clone (Three.js) · Contrato de Entrega

> Gran-Mestre · 2026-08-13 · Rota: COMPLEX · Versão 1.0

## 1. Objetivo

Jogo FPS completo estilo **DOOM (1993)** construído com **Three.js**, 100% procedural
(sem assets binários externos — texturas e sons gerados em runtime), leve o suficiente
para rodar fluido (~60 FPS) no navegador em hardware comum.

## 2. Requisitos Funcionais (do pedido do usuário)

| # | Requisito | Detalhe |
|---|-----------|---------|
| R1 | Tech stack | Three.js + JS (ES Modules) + HTML5 + CSS. Sem build step pesado (pode usar módulos ES nativos + import map). |
| R2 | Armas | **Pelo menos 4**: Pistola (hitscan), Shotgun (spread hitscan), Chaingun (full-auto hitscan), Rocket Launcher (projétil + splash). Alternância por roda do mouse / teclas 1-4. Munição e recuo por arma. |
| R3 | Inimigos | **Pelo menos 3**: (a) Zumbi/Former Human — hitscan fraco; (b) Imp — projétil de plasma; (c) Demon/Pinky — corpo-a-corpo veloz; bônus (d) Barão de Hell — mini-chefão tanque. IA: idle/chase/attack/morte. |
| R4 | Física detalhada | Aceleração/atrito no movimento, strafe, run; gravidade + pulo; colisão AABB por célula do grid (raycast DDA para hitscan e visão); colisão com inimigos (empurrar); splash damage com falloff por raio; view bobbing; portas animadas; projéteis sem gravidade com colisão contra grid e entidades. |
| R5 | Minimap | Overlay canvas 2D (canto) com mapa, paredes, posição do jogador, direção de visão, inimigos vistos/ativos. |
| R6 | HUD | Health, munição por arma, arma ativa, crosshair, dano recebido (flash), morte, mensagens de pickup, tela inicial + tela de vitória. |
| R7 | Itens | Health packs, ammo, armor — com bob e pickup. |
| R8 | Áudio | WebAudio **sintetizado** (tiros, hits, explosões, dano, pickup, morte, ambiência) — zero arquivos. |
| R9 | Assets leves | Tudo procedural: texturas via canvas, geometria low-poly, InstancedMesh para inimigos/projéteis, sem sombras caras, pixel ratio limitado, texturas pequenas (≤256px). Zero dependência externa além do three.module.js local (baixado para o projeto). |
| R10 | Jogável | Pointer Lock, mouse para olhar, correção de porte, dificuldade balanceada, vitória ao zerar o mapa (matar todos / alcançar saída). |
| R11 | Design | UI/HUD com qualidade de design (skill /shared/frontend) — estética militar-retrô coesa, tipografia legível, estados visuais claros. |
| R12 | Validação | Testes unitários (node, lógica pura separada da Three) + **QA real com Playwright**: abrir, navegar, atirar, matar inimigos, coletar itens, screenshot, FPS. |

## 3. Arquitetura (fisicamente separada: lógica pura ↔ render)

```
index.html            — shell + import map (three local)
css/style.css         — HUD, telas, minimap container, design system
js/constants.js       — ⚙️ puro: mapas, física, armas, inimigos, itens (tabelas de dados)
js/map.js             — ⚙️ puro: grid, parse, raycast DDA, linha de visão, portas (estado)
js/player-physics.js  — ⚙️ puro: movimento, colisão AABB, gravidade, pulo
js/weapons-core.js    — ⚙️ puro: dano, splash falloff, ammo, recuo (math)
js/engine.js          — 🎨 Three.js: renderer, cena, luzes, loop, instancing
js/level.js           — 🎨 constrói geometria do nível a partir do grid puro
js/player.js          — 🎨 câmera, input, aplica física, viewmodel
js/weapons.js         — 🎨 viewmodels (malhas procedurais), hitscan visual, projéteis
js/enemies.js         — 🎨 meshes de inimigos + IA (consome dados puros)
js/minimap.js         — 🎨 canvas 2D overlay
js/hud.js             — 🎨 DOM/CSS: barras, números, crosshair, telas
js/audio.js           — 🎨 WebAudio sintetizado
js/particles.js       — 🎨 sistema de partículas pool
js/main.js            — bootstrap + state machine (menu/playing/gameover/win)
tests/map.test.mjs        — grid + DDA + visão
tests/physics.test.mjs    — colisão/movimento
tests/weapons.test.mjs    — dano/splash/ammo
tests/level.test.mjs      — parse/render-data
```

⚠️ Arquivos marcados ⚙️ **não importam Three.js** (100% testáveis em node). 🎨 importam.

## 4. Física — especificação detalhada

| Parâmetro | Valor | Notas |
|-----------|-------|-------|
| Escala | 1 unidade ≈ 1 metro | Grid: célula de 1 u |
| Player radius | 0.40 u | AABB cilíndrica para colisão |
| Player altura | 1.80 u | eye height 1.62 u |
| Walk speed | 4.2 u/s | |
| Run (Shift) | 6.2 u/s | |
| Aceleração | ~1.4 s até topo | exponencial suave, Doom-feel |
| Atrito | decai ~4x/s | |
| Gravidade | 28 u/s² | |
| Jump velocity | 9.5 u/s | ≈ 1.6 u de altura |
| Colisão | swept por eixo (X e Z separados) | sliding contra paredes |
| Colisão inimigos | push suave (player mais pesado) | entraves de passagem |
| Hitscan range | 800 u | DDA contra grid + AABB inimigos |
| Splash | raio 6 u, falloff linear | auto-dano ativo |
| Projéteis | 6–14 u/s sem gravidade | rocket 10 u/s |
| Portas | animação 1.2 s, colidível | ativadas por proximidade/interação |
| View bob | seno 0.02 u @ step frequency | + recuo por arma |

## 5. Armas (DPS balanceado)

| Arma | Dano | Cadência | Spread | Munição | Notas |
|------|------|----------|--------|---------|-------|
| Pistola | 5–10 (7 pelotas=1) | 2.5/s | 0° | Infinita → balas | precisa, zoom leve |
| Shotgun | 7×0.5 (5 pelotas) | 0.9/s | ±4° | Balas 8/peca | alto burst |
| Chaingun | 4–7 | 9/s | ±2° | Balas | full-auto |
| Rocket | 60–90 (+splash) | 0.55/s | 0° | Foguetes | auto-dano, área |

## 6. Inimigos

| Nome | HP | Dano | Velocidade | Tipo | Recompensa |
|------|----|------|------------|------|-----------|
| Zumbi | 20 | 3–8 | 2.0 | hitscan 8/s | balas |
| Imp | 60 | 8–16 | 3.0 | projétil 3 u/s | balas |
| Demon (Pinky) | 150 | 10–20 | 4.5 | melee | balas |
| Barão | 400 | 15–24 | 2.2 | projétil duplo | health/armor |

IA: estados `IDLE(0) → CHASE → ATTACK`; visão por cone 60° + linha-de-visão DDA;
distância de aggro 14 u; mantém distância ótima por arma; morte → partículas + drop.

## 7. Mapa

Grid textual 24×24 com legendas: `#` parede, `.` chão, `P` spawn player,
`Z/I/D/B` spawns inimigos, `H/A/M` itens (health/armor/ammo), `E` porta, `>` saída.
Layout: arena principal + corredores + sala chefe. Texturas procedurais:
startan (vermelho), tech (cinza), brick, emblema (logo). Teto/chão com variação.

## 8. Qualidade & Critérios de Trânsito (R28)

- Testes unitários node P/GGEM → `PASSOU_CATEGORICO` (todos verdes).
- QA Playwright real (R29): jogo abre, pointer lock, dispara, HUD atualiza,
  inimigo morre, dano funciona, minimap renderiza, FPS ≥ 30 em screenshot.
- Verificação visual (R30): screenshots avaliados — estética coerente, sem
  artefatos, HUD legível.
- Arquivos ≤ 400 linhas, funções ≤ 50 linhas, sem console.log, zero segredos.

## 9. Não-escopo (v1)

- Sem multiplayer, sem save/load, sem sistema de níveis múltiplos (1 mapa master),
  sem assets binários/GLTF externos, sem shadows real-time pesadas.

## 1. Architecture (the old game — full Three.js, ES modules, no bundler)

- **Stack**: HTML5 + ES modules (`import`/`export`), Three.js `0.160.0` via CDN importmap (`https://unpkg.com/three@0.160.0/build/three.module.js`), served via `python3 -m http.server` (ES modules don't load from `file://`).
- **Module registry pattern**: each JS module self-registers via `window.__registerMod(name, { init, update })`; `main.js` boots them in deterministic order `['level','player','enemies','weapons','particles','game','hud','minimap','audio']` (plus non-module `engine.js`, `constants.js`, `move.js`).
- **State**: global `window.__game = { state, events, stats, mods, level, player, enemies, weapons }` — modules communicate only via this + `game.events` callbacks (`onShot/onHit/onKill/onPickup/onDoor/onSecret/onDamage/onDeath/onExit/onMessage/onExplosion/onEnemyAttack/onEnemyProjectileHit/onNoAmmo/onSwitch`). Defensive `?.` everywhere.
- **FSM screens**: `MENU → PLAYING → PAUSED/DEAD/COMPLETE` (DOM overlays toggled by `id.toUpperCase() === state`; HUD visible in PLAYING+PAUSED). `DEAD ≡ GAME_OVER`. Pause on pointer-lock loss (ESC). Restart = `location.reload()`.
- **Engine** (`engine.js`): `WebGLRenderer` with `antialias`, `powerPreference:'high-performance'`, pixelRatio cap 1.75; `PerspectiveCamera` fov 75, near 0.1, far 120, `rotation.order='YXZ'`; fog `Fog(0x12121c, 25, 95)`; input = `Set` of key codes + edge-triggered `pressed` set + pointer-lock mouse (sens 0.0022) + keyboard turn fallback (Q/E/arrows, 2.4 rad/s) + pitch clamp ±(π/2−0.05). `wasPressed(code)` is edge-trigger. dt clamped to 0.05.
- **No physics engine** — deterministic AABB-vs-grid collision with per-axis slide (see §4).
- **Perf budget**: fog for draw distance, PointLights only on 6 torches (flicker via `sin`), particle pool of 80, no textures (flat `MeshStandardMaterial` vertex-color zones), ceiling as single BackSide plane.

- **Movement model**: exponential smoothing — `vel += (targetVel − vel) * min(1, accel*dt*air)`; friction decay when no input & grounded; jump sets `vel.y = 8.5`; gravity integrates; ground when `pos.y ≤ eye`.
- **Collision**: circle-vs-grid AABB resolved **per axis** (X then Z), with a probe at `pos ± radius*sign`; on hit, snap back to `before` on that axis and zero velocity → slide along walls. Out-of-bounds = solid.
- **`moveVec(yaw, ix, iz)`** (pure function in `move.js`, bugfix target): local→world `x = ix*cos + iz*sin`, `z = −ix*sin + iz*cos`. **This was the mirrored-movement bug**: earlier `player.js` used `R_y(−yaw)` so W walked backwards when turned 90°; fixed by extracting this pure function + TDD tests.
- **Damage model**: armor absorbs 33% (armor -= absorbed, hp -= rest); lava deals `15*dt` per second (and 5 dmg random in game.js); invulnerability 1 s post-hit; death → hp 0 → `alive=false` → event → DEAD screen. 5: import * as THREE from 'three';

19: const canvas = document.getElementById('game-canvas');
20: const engine = createEngine(canvas);

23: engine.scene.add(level.group);

25: const player = createPlayer(engine, map);

33:   damagePlayer: (d) => applyDamage(d),
34:   onImpact: (x, y, z, type) => {
35:     if (type === 'rocket') {
36:       particles.fire(x, y, z, 14);
37:       particles.smoke(x, y, z, 8);

40:     } else {
41:       particles.fire(x, y, z, 8);
42:       audio?.play('hit');
43:     }
44:   },
45:   sparks: (x, y, z, n, color) => particles.sparks(x, y, z, n, color),
46: });
47: 
48: const enemies = createEnemies(engine.scene, map, {
49:   getPlayer: () => player,
50:   damagePlayer: (d) => applyDamage(d),
51:   spawnFireball: (x, y, z, dx, dz, owner) => projectiles.spawn('fireball', x, y, z, dx, dz, owner),
52:   meleeImpact: (x, z) => { particles.blood(x, 1, z, 6); audio?.play('hit'); },
53:   onKill: (en, x, z) => {

57:     dropFrom(en, x, z);
58:   },
59: });

62:   map,
63:   getEnemies: () => enemies.list,
64:   shoot: () => audio?.play('shot'),
65:   noAmmo: () => audio?.play('noammo'),
66:   spawnProjectile: (o, dir) => projectiles.spawn('rocket', o.x, o.y, o.z, dir.x, dir.z),
67:   impact: (x, y, z) => { particles.sparks(x, y, z, 4); audio?.play('hit'); },
68: });

72: }));

81: const pickupMeshes = [];

84:   armor: new THREE.BoxGeometry(0.34, 0.34, 0.34),

tool_input.description: Fix audio module e tiro mouse
tool_input.prompt:
Two more real bugs found in the Three.js game at `/mnt/dados/projetos/doom test`. Fix them:

**Bug A — `audio?.play is not a function` (crash on any kill/explosion):**
`js/audio.js` registers `window.__registerMod('audio', { init() { ... creates window.__game.audio = { play, toggleMute } ... } })`. But `js/main.js` line 27 does `const audio = window.__mods?.audio;` — which is the module object `{ init }`, which has NO `play`/`toggleMute` methods. So `audio?.play('kill')` throws "audio?.play is not a function" (seen in QA when killAll runs). Fix: the registered module itself must expose `play` and `toggleMute` directly, e.g.:
```js
window.__registerMod('audio', {
  play: (n) => SFX[n]?.(),
  toggleMute: () => { muted = !muted; return muted; },
  init() { ensure(); window.__game.audio = { play: (n) => SFX[n]?.(), toggleMute: () => { muted = !muted; return muted; } }; },
});
```
Keep `init()` working (it resumes/creates the AudioContext on user gesture via btn-start click). The `toggleMute()` on the module should return the new muted state so `window.__game.toggleMute()` works.

**Bug B — player can NEVER shoot (mouse click does nothing):**
`js/weapons.js` `update(dt)` only checks keys 1-4 (select weapon) and scroll (cycle weapon). It NEVER fires on mouse. `fire()` exists (line 109) but nothing calls it. `js/main.js` only calls `weapons.update(dt)` in the loop. Fix: inside `weapons.update(dt)`, add mouse firing — full-auto respecting the weapon cadence (`fire()` already guards with `canFire` + `fireReady`, which consume ammo and respect rate):
```js
if (engine.input.keys.has('Mouse0')) fire();
```
Place it near the end of update(), after the scroll/select block. Note `engine.input.keys` is a Set — 'Mouse0' is added on mousedown and removed on mouseup (engine.js lines 40-45), so holding the button fires continuously at the weapon's fire rate, and clicking fires once.

Then verify:
- `node --check js/audio.js js/weapons.js` passes.
- `node --test tests/*.test.mjs` — all 36 tests still pass (do NOT modify tests or pure logic).
- Server on :8765 still responds (restart if needed, same as before).
- Quick sanity with `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://localhost:8765/`.

Report: files changed, exact diff summary, check results, test count, server status.

4: import { C } from './constants.js';

6: /* Dano de splash com falloff linear: dmg*(1 - d/radius) + 1, mínimo 1. */
7: export function splashDamage(w, centerDist, radius = C.WEAPONS.rocket.splash) {
8:   if (centerDist >= radius) return 1;
9:   return w.damage * (1 - centerDist / radius) + 1;

18: export function spreadOffset(spread) {
19:   return {
20:     a: (Math.random() * 2 - 1) * spread,
21:     b: (Math.random() * 2 - 1) * spread,
22:   };
23: }
24: 
25: /* Dispersão efetiva do chaingun: base + crescimento por tiro contínuo. */
26: export function chaingunSpread(base, spin) {
27:   return base + spin * C.WEAPONS.chaingun.spreadGrow;
28: }
29: 
30: /* Cooldown pronto? */
31: export function fireReady(w, sinceLast) {
32:   return sinceLast >= w.rate;
33: }
34: 
35: /* Pode disparar? Pistola é infinita; demais exigem munição. */
36: export function canFire(w, ammo) {
37:   if (w.ammoType === 'pistol') return true;
38:   return (ammo[w.ammoType] || 0) > 0;
39: }

41: /* Consome munição (imutável — retorna novo objeto). */
42: export function consumeAmmo(w, ammo) {
43:   if (w.ammoType === 'pistol') return ammo;
44:   const t = w.ammoType;
45:   return { ...ammo, [t]: Math.max(0, (ammo[t] || 0) - (w.ammoPerShot || 1)) };

Structural bug in `/mnt/dados/projetos/doom test/js/player.js` — the player has TWO divergent states, breaking damage/death/gameover and teleport.

Root cause: `createPlayer` ends with `return { ...player, camera, update, damage, heal, addArmor, isLookingAt };`. The spread `...player` copies the primitive VALUES (`x, z, health, armor, invuln, dead, kills, bob, ...`) into a NEW object at creation time. From then on:
- `damage()`/`heal()`/`addArmor()`/physics (`update`) mutate the CLOSURE object `player` (real state).
- `main.js`/HUD/debug API use the RETURNED object (frozen copies): `teleport(x,z)` changes the copy's x/z but physics still uses the closure → player never actually moves; `applyDamage` reads `player.dead` from the copy (always false) → `setState('gameover')` NEVER fires even after fatal damage; `enemies` chase the frozen copy coordinates; HUD shows stale health.

Fix (minimal, keeps same API): return the SAME object the closures mutate, with the methods attached via `Object.assign`. Replace the return statement with:
```js
return Object.assign(player, {
  camera,
  update,
  damage,
  heal,
  addArmor,
  isLookingAt,
});
```

4: import * as THREE from 'three';
5: import { C } from './constants.js';
6: 
7: const MAX = C.PARTICLES.max;
8: 
9: export function createParticles(scene) {
10:   const positions = new Float32Array(MAX * 3);
11:   const colors = new Float32Array(MAX * 3);
12:   const sizes = new Float32Array(MAX);
13:   const geo = new THREE.BufferGeometry();
14:   geo.setAttribute('position', new THREE.BufferAttribute(positions, 3));
15:   geo.setAttribute('color', new THREE.BufferAttribute(colors, 3));
16:   geo.setAttribute('size', new THREE.BufferAttribute(sizes, 1));
17: 
18:   const mat = new THREE.PointsMaterial({
19:     size: 0.12,
20:     vertexColors: true,
21:     transparent: true,
22:     opacity: 0.9,
23:     depthWrite: false,
24:     blending: THREE.AdditiveBlending,
25:   });
26:   const points = new THREE.Points(geo, mat);
27:   points.frustumCulled = false;
28:   scene.add(points);
29: 
30:   const pool = [];
31:   for (let i = 0; i < MAX; i++) {
32:     pool.push({
33:       active: false,
34:       life: 0,
35:       maxLife: 1,
36:       vx: 0, vy: 0, vz: 0,
37:       r: 1, g: 1, b: 1,
38:       size: 0.1,
39:       gravity: 0,
40:     });
41:   }
42: 
43:   let cursor = 0;
44: 
45:   function emit(x, y, z, opts = {}) {
46:     const p = pool[cursor];
47:     cursor = (cursor + 1) % MAX;
48:     p.active = true;
49:     p.life = p.maxLife = opts.life ?? 0.5;
50:     p.vx = opts.vx ?? (Math.random() - 0.5) * 2;
51:     p.vy = opts.vy ?? Math.random() * 2;
52:     p.vz = opts.vz ?? (Math.random() - 0.5) * 2;
53:     p.r = opts.r ?? 1; p.g = opts.g ?? 1; p.b = opts.b ?? 1;
54:     p.size = opts.size ?? 0.1;
55:     p.gravity = opts.gravity ?? 0;
56:     positions[p._i * 3] = x;
57:     positions[p._i * 3 + 1] = y;
58:     positions[p._i * 3 + 2] = z;
59:   }
60: 
61:   pool.forEach((p, i) => { p._i = i; });
62: 
63:   function sparks(x, y, z, n = 6, color = 0xffcc44) {
64:     const c = new THREE.Color(color);
65:     for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
66:       emit(x, y, z, {
67:         life: 0.3 + Math.random() * 0.3,
68:         vx: (Math.random() - 0.5) * 6,
69:         vy: Math.random() * 4,
70:         vz: (Math.random() - 0.5) * 6,
71:         r: c.r, g: c.g, b: c.b,
72:         size: 0.06,
73:         gravity: -6,
74:       });
75:     }
76:   }
77: 
78:   function blood(x, y, z, n = 8) {
79:     for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
80:       emit(x, y, z, {
81:         life: 0.4 + Math.random() * 0.4,
82:         vx: (Math.random() - 0.5) * 3,
83:         vy: Math.random() * 2.5,
84:         vz: (Math.random() - 0.5) * 3,
85:         r: 0.7, g: 0.05, b: 0.05,
86:         size: 0.09,
87:         gravity: -8,
88:       });
89:     }
90:   }
91: 
92:   function fire(x, y, z, n = 10) {
93:     for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
94:       const t = Math.random();
95:       emit(x, y, z, {
96:         life: 0.3 + Math.random() * 0.4,
97:         vx: (Math.random() - 0.5) * 1.5,
98:         vy: 2 + Math.random() * 2,
99:         vz: (Math.random() - 0.5) * 1.5,
100:         r: 1, g: 0.5 + t * 0.4, b: 0.1,
101:         size: 0.15,
102:         gravity: 0,
103:       });
104:     }
105:   }
106: 
107:   function smoke(x, y, z, n = 6) {
108:     for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
109:       emit(x, y, z, {
110:         life: 0.8 + Math.random() * 0.6,
111:         vx: (Math.random() - 0.5) * 1,
112:         vy: 1.5 + Math.random() * 1.5,
113:         vz: (Math.random() - 0.5) * 1,
114:         r: 0.4, g: 0.4, b: 0.42,
115:         size: 0.22,
116:         gravity: 0,
117:       });
118:     }
119:   }
120: 
121:   function update(dt) {
122:     for (const p of pool) {
123:       if (!p.active) continue;
124:       p.life -= dt;
125:       if (p.life <= 0) {
126:         p.active = false;
127:         positions[p._i * 3 + 1] = -999;
128:         continue;
129:       }
130:       p.vy += p.gravity * dt;
131:       positions[p._i * 3] += p.vx * dt;
132:       positions[p._i * 3 + 1] += p.vy * dt;
133:       positions[p._i * 3 + 2] += p.vz * dt;
134:       const fade = p.life / p.maxLife;
135:       colors[p._i * 3] = p.r * fade;
136:       colors[p._i * 3 + 1] = p.g * fade;
137:       colors[p._i * 3 + 2] = p.b * fade;
138:       sizes[p._i] = p.size * fade;
139:     }
140:     geo.attributes.position.needsUpdate = true;
141:     geo.attributes.color.needsUpdate = true;
142:     geo.attributes.size.needsUpdate = true;
143:   }
144:

/* weapons.js — viewmodels procedurais (DOOM-style), recuo com mola, muzzle flash,
 * ejeção de cápsulas, fumaça de foguete, animação de troca de arma.
 * 🎨 Render: THREE (malhas presas à câmera) + weapons-core.js (math pura).
 * Disparos de projétil delegam ao módulo de projectiles via hook.
 */
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { C } from './constants.js';
import { fireReady, canFire, consumeAmmo, spreadOffset, chaingunSpread } from './weapons-core.js';
import { raycastWall } from './map.js';

const KEYS = ['1', '2', '3', '4'];
const NAMES = ['pistol', 'shotgun', 'chaingun', 'rocket'];

// Constantes de animação (mola crítico-amortecida p/ o recuo).
const KICK_SPRING = 300;
const KICK_DAMP = 2 * Math.sqrt(KICK_SPRING);
const BASE_X = 0.26, BASE_Y = -0.24, BASE_Z = -0.45;
const SWITCH_OUT = 0.09, SWITCH_IN = 0.1;

const easeIn = (k) => k * k;
const easeOut = (k) => 1 - (1 - k) * (1 - k);

export function createWeapons(engine, player, scene, hooks) {
  let ammo = { shell: C.WEAPONS.shotgun.ammoStart, bullet: C.WEAPONS.chaingun.ammoStart, rocket: C.WEAPONS.rocket.ammoStart };
  let current = 0;
  let sinceLast = 99;
  let kick = 0, kickV = 0, lift = 0, liftV = 0;
  let muzzleT = 0;
  let spin = 0;
  let firingT = 0;
  let spinVel = 0;
  let slideBack = 0, pumpBack = 0;
  let switchState = null; // { phase:'out'|'in', t, from, to }

  const camera = engine.camera;
  const viewGroup = new THREE.Group();
  camera.add(viewGroup);
  scene.add(camera);

  const materials = {
    dark: new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: 0x2a2d33, roughness: 0.6, metalness: 0.35 }),
    steel: new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: 0x7a8189, roughness: 0.32, metalness: 0.85 }),
    grip: new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: 0x3f2f1e, roughness: 0.85, metalness: 0.0 }),
    brass: new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: 0xb08a3a, roughness: 0.3, metalness: 0.9 }),
    accent: new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: 0x4db8ff, emissive: 0x1a6a99, emissiveIntensity: 0.9, roughness: 0.4, metalness: 0.4 }),
  };

  function mesh(geo, mat, x = 0, y = 0, z = 0, rx = 0, ry = 0, rz = 0) {
    const m = new THREE.Mesh(geo, mat);
    m.position.set(x, y, z);
    m.rotation.set(rx, ry, rz);
    return m;
  }
  function box(w, h, d, mat, x, y, z, rx = 0, rz = 0) {
    return mesh(new THREE.BoxGeometry(w, h, d), materials[mat], x, y, z, rx, 0, rz);
  }
  function cyl(rTop, rBot, h, seg, mat, x, y, z) {
    return mesh(new THREE.CylinderGeometry(rTop, rBot, h, seg), materials[mat], x, y, z, Math.PI / 2);
  }

  function buildViewmodel(type) {
    const g = new THREE.Group();
    g.userData = { tip: new THREE.Vector3(0, 0.05, -0.32) };
    if (type === 'pistol') {
      const slide = box(0.072, 0.095, 0.22, 'steel', 0, 0.025, -0.02);
      g.add(slide);
      g.add(cyl(0.028, 0.028, 0.14, 8, 'dark', 0, 0.04, -0.18));
      g.add(box(0.068, 0.085, 0.15, 'dark', 0, -0.02, 0.07));
      const grip = box(0.07, 0.14, 0.09, 'grip', 0, -0.105, 0.11, 0, 0.08);
      g.add(grip);
      g.add(box(0.012, 0.022, 0.01, 'dark', 0, 0.095, -0.15)); // mira dianteira
      g.add(box(0.024, 0.016, 0.014, 'dark', 0, 0.09, 0.0));   // mira traseira
      g.userData.slide = slide;
      g.userData.slideZ = slide.position.z;
      g.userData.tip.set(0, 0.05, -0.3);
    } else if (type === 'shotgun') {
      g.add(cyl(0.032, 0.032, 0.5, 10, 'steel', 0, 0.015, -0.12));
      g.add(cyl(0.022, 0.022, 0.42, 8, 'dark', 0, -0.045, -0.1));
      const pump = box(0.07, 0.052, 0.12, 'grip', 0, -0.045, -0.02);
      g.add(pump);
      g.add(box(0.09, 0.1, 0.2, 'dark', 0, 0.02, 0.16));
      g.add(box(0.07, 0.1, 0.17, 'grip', 0, -0.005, 0.33, 0, 0.06)); // coronha
      g.add(cyl(0.045, 0.045, 0.05, 8, 'dark', 0, 0.015, -0.38));    // boca
      g.add(box(0.012, 0.012, 0.012, 'accent', 0, 0.055, -0.36));    // bead de mira
      g.userData.pump = pump;
      g.userData.pumpZ = pump.position.z;
      g.userData.tip.set(0, 0.02, -0.42);
    } else if (type === 'chaingun') {
      const barrels = new THREE.Group();
      for (let a = 0; a < 3; a++) {
        const ang = (a / 3) * Math.PI * 2;
        const b = cyl(0.028, 0.028, 0.32, 6, 'steel', Math.cos(ang) * 0.055, Math.sin(ang) * 0.055, -0.3);
        barrels.add(b);
      }
      g.add(barrels);
      g.add(box(0.16, 0.16, 0.42, 'dark', 0, 0, 0.02));
      g.add(cyl(0.078, 0.078, 0.14, 10, 'steel', 0, 0, -0.14)); // guarda do cano
      g.add(box(0.12, 0.06, 0.1, 'dark', 0, 0.11, 0.06));       // alimentador
      g.add(box(0.08, 0.1, 0.12, 'grip', 0, -0.13, 0.2));
      g.add(box(0.02, 0.02, 0.02, 'accent', 0, 0.125, -0.24));  // indicador emissivo
      g.userData.barrels = barrels;
      g.userData.tip.set(0, 0.02, -0.46);
    } else {
      g.add(cyl(0.075, 0.075, 0.55, 10, 'dark', 0, 0, -0.08));
      g.add(cyl(0.09, 0.09, 0.06, 10, 'steel', 0, 0, -0.36));   // boca
      g.add(cyl(0.078, 0.078, 0.03, 10, 'accent', 0, 0, 0.02)); // anel emissivo
      g.add(box(0.014, 0.06, 0.02, 'steel', 0.06, 0.075, -0.12)); // mira frontal
      g.add(box(0.05, 0.06, 0.014, 'steel', 0, 0.075, 0.06));    // mira traseira
      g.add(box(0.06, 0.09, 0.18, 'grip', 0, -0.03, 0.34));      // coronha
      g.add(box(0.06, 0.09, 0.1, 'grip', 0, -0.11, 0.2));        // punho
      g.add(box(0.05, 0.05, 0.08, 'dark', 0, -0.09, 0.29));      // apoio de ombro
      g.userData.tip.set(0, 0.03, -0.42);
    }
    g.position.set(BASE_X, BASE_Y, BASE_Z);
    return g;
  }

  const viewmodels = NAMES.map((n) => {
    const g = buildViewmodel(n);
    g.visible = false;
    viewGroup.add(g);
    return g;
  });
  viewmodels[0].visible = true;

  // Muzzle flash (plano brilhante aditivo + luz pontual que some rápido).
  const muzzle = new THREE.Mesh(
    new THREE.PlaneGeometry(0.16, 0.16),
    new THREE.MeshBasicMaterial({ color: 0xffd873, transparent: true, opacity: 0.95, blending: THREE.AdditiveBlending, depthWrite: false, side: THREE.DoubleSide }),
  );
  muzzle.visible = false;
  viewGroup.add(muzzle);
  const muzzleLight = new THREE.PointLight(0xffb84d, 0, 7);
  viewGroup.add(muzzleLight);

  // Partículas (cápsulas + fumaça).
  const casings = [];
  const smokes = [];
  const smokeMat = new THREE.MeshBasicMaterial({ color: 0x9a9a9a, transparent: true, opacity: 0.65 });
  function spawnCasing(pos) {
    const c = new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.BoxGeometry(0.02, 0.02, 0.035), materials.brass.clone());
    c.material.transparent = true;
    c.position.copy(pos);
    c.velocity = new THREE.Vector3(0.55 + Math.random() * 0.35, 0.55 + Math.random() * 0.3, -0.2 - Math.random() * 0.2);
    c.angVel = new THREE.Vector3(Math.random() * 9, Math.random() * 9, Math.random() * 9);
    c.life = 0.9;
    viewGroup.add(c);
    casings.push(c);
  }
  function spawnSmoke(pos) {
    const s = new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.SphereGeometry(0.045 + Math.random() * 0.03, 6, 6), smokeMat.clone());
    s.position.copy(pos);
    s.velocity = new THREE.Vector3((Math.random() - 0.5) * 0.3, 0.25 + Math.random() * 0.25, (Math.random() - 0.5) * 0.3 - 0.25);
    s.grow = 0.45 + Math.random() * 0.5;
    s.life = 0.6;
    viewGroup.add(s);
    smokes.push(s);
  }

  const camDir = () => {
    const e = new THREE.Euler(camera.rotation.x, camera.rotation.y, 0, 'YXZ');
    const q = new THREE.Quaternion().setFromEuler(e);
    const v = new THREE.Vector3(0, 0, -1).applyQuaternion(q);
    return v;
  };

  function hitscanDamage(w, count = 1) { ... unchanged ... }

  function fire() { ... unchanged core + fx ... }

  function select(i) {
    if (i === current && !switchState) return;
    if (switchState) { // interrompe troca em andamento
      current = switchState.to;
      viewmodels.forEach((gg, k) => { gg.visible = k === current; });
      switchState = null;
    }
    switchState = { phase: 'out', t: 0, from: current, to: i };
  }

  function update(dt) {
    sinceLast += dt;
    // muzzle flash
    if (muzzleT > 0) {
      muzzleT -= dt;
      const vm = viewmodels[current];
      const tip = vm.userData.tip;
      muzzle.visible = true;
      muzzle.position.set(tip.x, tip.y, tip.z);
      muzzle.rotation.z += dt * 4;
      muzzleLight.position.set(tip.x, tip.y, tip.z);
      muzzleLight.intensity = 9 * Math.max(0, muzzleT / 0.045);
    } else {
      muzzle.visible = false;
      muzzleLight.intensity = 0;
    }

    // recuo com mola (criticamente amortecido)
    kick += kickV * dt;
    kickV += (-kick * KICK_SPRING - kickV * KICK_DAMP) * dt;
    lift += liftV * dt;
    liftV += (-lift * KICK_SPRING - liftV * KICK_DAMP) * dt;
    if (kick <= 0.001) { kick = 0; kickV = Math.max(0, kickV); }
    if (lift <= 0.001) { lift = 0; liftV = Math.max(0, liftV); }
    firingT = Math.max(0, firingT - dt);
    slideBack = Math.max(0, slideBack - dt * 0.22);
    pumpBack = Math.max(0, pumpBack - dt * 0.16);

    // troca de arma
    if (switchState) {
      switchState.t += dt;
      if (switchState.phase === 'out' && switchState.t >= SWITCH_OUT) {
        current = switchState.to;
        viewmodels.forEach((gg, k) => { gg.visible = k === current; });
        kickV += 0.8; liftV += 0.15;
        switchState = { phase: 'in', t: 0, from: null, to: current };
      } else if (switchState.phase === 'in' && switchState.t >= SWITCH_IN) {
        switchState = null;
      }
    }

    const bob = Math.sin(player.bob * Math.PI * 2) * 0.008;
    for (const g of viewmodels) {
      if (!g.visible) continue;
      let sy = 0, sz = 0, srx = 0;
      if (switchState && switchState.phase === 'out' && g === viewmodels[switchState.from]) {
        const e = easeIn(Math.min(1, switchState.t / SWITCH_OUT));
        sy = -0.34 * e; sz = 0.3 * e; srx = 0.55 * e;
      } else if (switchState && switchState.phase === 'in' && g === viewmodels[switchState.to]) {
        const e = easeOut(Math.min(1, switchState.t / SWITCH_IN));
        sy = -0.34 * (1 - e); sz = 0.3 * (1 - e); srx = 0.55 * (1 - e);
      }
      g.position.z = BASE_Z + kick * 0.28 + sz;
      g.position.y = BASE_Y + lift * 0.05 + bob + sy;
      g.rotation.x = kick * 0.25 + lift * 0.12 + srx;
      if (NAMES[current] === 'chaingun') {
        g.rotation.z = Math.sin(performance.now() * 0.05) * 0.02;
      }
      // animações de peças
      if (g.userData.slide) g.userData.slide.position.z = g.userData.slideZ + slideBack;
      if (g.userData.pump) g.userData.pump.position.z = g.userData.pumpZ + pumpBack;
      if (g.userData.barrels) {
        spinVel = firingT > 0
          ? Math.min(spinVel + 320 * dt, 46)
          : Math.max(0, spinVel - 140 * dt);
        g.userData.barrels.rotation.z += spinVel * dt;
      }
    }

    // cápsulas
    for (let i = casings.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
      const c = casings[i];
      c.velocity.y -= 4.2 * dt;
      c.position.addScaledVector(c.velocity, dt);
      c.rotation.x += c.angVel.x * dt;
      c.rotation.y += c.angVel.y * dt;
      c.rotation.z += c.angVel.z * dt;
      c.life -= dt;
      c.material.opacity = Math.max(0, c.life / 0.9);
      if (c.life <= 0) { viewGroup.remove(c); casings.splice(i, 1); }
    }
    // fumaça
    for (let i = smokes.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
      const s = smokes[i];
      s.position.addScaledVector(s.velocity, dt);
      s.velocity.multiplyScalar(Math.max(0, 1 - dt * 2.5));
      const k = s.life / 0.6;
      s.scale.setScalar(1 + (1 - k) * s.grow);

```js
function hexRgb(hex) {
  const n = parseInt(hex.slice(1), 16);
  return [(n >> 16) & 255, (n >> 8) & 255, n & 255];
}

function grimePass(ctx, w, h, t, strength = 0.08, seed = 7) {
  const img = ctx.getImageData(0, 0, w, h);
  const d = img.data;
  const base = hexRgb(t.base);
  for (let y = 0; y < h; y++) {
    for (let x = 0; x < w; x++) {
      const r = hash2(x, y, seed);
      if (r > strength) continue;
      const i = (y * w + x) * 4;
      const f = 0.65 + hash2(x, y, seed + 1) * 0.5; // 0.65..1.15 escurece/clareia levemente
      d[i] = Math.max(0, Math.min(255, d[i] * f));
      d[i+1] = Math.max(0, Math.min(255, d[i+1] * f));
      d[i+2] = Math.max(0, Math.min(255, d[i+2] * f));
    }
  }
  ctx.putImageData(img, 0, 0);
}
```

/* particles.js — pool de partículas: faíscas, sangue, fogo, fumaça, muzzle flash.
 * 🎨 Render: sprites Three (Points) com vida curta, sem alocação por frame.
 * Dois sistemas de blend: aditivo (fogo/faíscas/muzzle) e normal (sangue/fumaça).
 */
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { C } from './constants.js';

const MAX = C.PARTICLES.max;

// Sprite suave (círculo radial) — gerado via canvas quando disponível (browser).
function makeSprite() {
  if (typeof document === 'undefined') return null;
  const c = document.createElement('canvas');
  c.width = c.height = 32;
  const ctx = c.getContext('2d');
  const g = ctx.createRadialGradient(16, 16, 0, 16, 16, 16);
  g.addColorStop(0, 'rgba(255,255,255,1)');
  g.addColorStop(0.35, 'rgba(255,255,255,0.85)');
  g.addColorStop(1, 'rgba(255,255,255,0)');
  ctx.fillStyle = g;
  ctx.fillRect(0, 0, 32, 32);
  return new THREE.CanvasTexture(c);
}

const SPRITE = makeSprite();

function makeSystem(scene, { blending, opacity = 1 }) {
  const positions = new Float32Array(MAX * 3);
  const colors = new Float32Array(MAX * 3);
  const sizes = new Float32Array(MAX);
  const geo = new THREE.BufferGeometry();
  geo.setAttribute('position', new THREE.BufferAttribute(positions, 3));
  geo.setAttribute('color', new THREE.BufferAttribute(colors, 3));
  geo.setAttribute('size', new THREE.BufferAttribute(sizes, 1));

  const mat = new THREE.PointsMaterial({
    size: 0.12,
    vertexColors: true,
    transparent: true,
    opacity,
    depthWrite: false,
    sizeAttenuation: true,
    blending,
    map: SPRITE || undefined,
  });
  const points = new THREE.Points(geo, mat);
  points.frustumCulled = false;
  scene.add(points);

  const pool = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < MAX; i++) {
    pool.push({
      active: false,
      life: 0,
      maxLife: 1,
      vx: 0, vy: 0, vz: 0,
      r: 1, g: 1, b: 1,
      size: 0.1,
      grow: 0,
      gravity: 0,
      drag: 0,
    });
  }
  pool.forEach((p, i) => { p._i = i; });

  let cursor = 0;

  function emit(x, y, z, opts = {}) {
    const p = pool[cursor];
    cursor = (cursor + 1) % MAX;
    p.active = true;
    p.life = p.maxLife = opts.life ?? 0.5;
    p.vx = opts.vx ?? (Math.random() - 0.5) * 2;
    p.vy = opts.vy ?? Math.random() * 2;
    p.vz = opts.vz ?? (Math.random() - 0.5) * 2;
    p.r = opts.r ?? 1; p.g = opts.g ?? 1; p.b = opts.b ?? 1;
    p.size = opts.size ?? 0.1;
    p.grow = opts.grow ?? 0;
    p.gravity = opts.gravity ?? 0;
    p.drag = opts.drag ?? 0;
    positions[p._i * 3] = x;
    positions[p._i * 3 + 1] = y;
    positions[p._i * 3 + 2] = z;
  }

  function update(dt) {
    for (const p of pool) {
      if (!p.active) continue;
      p.life -= dt;
      if (p.life <= 0) {
        p.active = false;
        positions[p._i * 3 + 1] = -999;
        continue;
      }
      p.vy += p.gravity * dt;
      if (p.drag > 0) {
        const d = Math.max(0, 1 - p.drag * dt);
        p.vx *= d; p.vy *= d; p.vz *= d;
      }
      positions[p._i * 3] += p.vx * dt;
      positions[p._i * 3 + 1] += p.vy * dt;
      positions[p._i * 3 + 2] += p.vz * dt;
      const fade = p.life / p.maxLife;
      colors[p._i * 3] = p.r * fade;
      colors[p._i * 3 + 1] = p.g * fade;
      colors[p._i * 3 + 2] = p.b * fade;
      sizes[p._i] = p.size + p.grow * (1 - fade);
    }
    geo.attributes.position.needsUpdate = true;
    geo.attributes.color.needsUpdate = true;
    geo.attributes.size.needsUpdate = true;
  }

  return { emit, update };
}

  const x = Math.sin(i * 127.1 + 311.7) * 43758.5453;
  return (x - Math.floor(x)) * Math.PI * 2;
}

function categoryOf(type) {
  if (type === 'health') return 'health';
  if (type === 'armor') return 'armor';
  if (type === 'shotgun' || type === 'chaingun' || type === 'rocket') return 'weapon';
  return 'ammo';
}

// Geometrias por categoria (uma Mesh por pickup).
function buildGeometry(cat) {
  switch (cat) {
    case 'health': {
      // cruz verde: 2D cross extrudado
      const s = 0.34, t = 0.11, d = 0.1;
      const shape = new THREE.Shape();
      shape.moveTo(-t / 2, s / 2);
      shape.lineTo(t / 2, s / 2);
      shape.lineTo(t / 2, t / 2);
      shape.lineTo(s / 2, t / 2);
      shape.lineTo(s / 2, -t / 2);
      shape.lineTo(t / 2, -t / 2);
      shape.lineTo(t / 2, -s / 2);
      shape.lineTo(-t / 2, -s / 2);
      shape.lineTo(-t / 2, -t / 2);
      shape.lineTo(-s / 2, -t / 2);
      shape.lineTo(-s / 2, t / 2);
      shape.lineTo(-t / 2, t / 2);
      shape.closePath();
      return new THREE.ExtrudeGeometry(shape, { depth: d, bevelEnabled: false });
    }
    case 'armor': {
      // escudo azul: placa hexagonal fina
      const w = 0.4, h = 0.46, d = 0.08;
      const shape = new THREE.Shape();
      shape.moveTo(-w / 2, -h / 2);
      shape.lineTo(-w / 2, 0);
      shape.quadraticCurveTo(-w / 2, h / 2, 0, h / 2);
      shape.quadraticCurveTo(w / 2, h / 2, w / 2, 0);
      shape.lineTo(w / 2, -h / 2);
      shape.lineTo(w * 0.35, -h / 2);
      shape.lineTo(0, -h / 2 + h * 0.22);
      shape.lineTo(-w * 0.35, -h / 2);
      shape.closePath();
      return new THREE.ExtrudeGeometry(shape, { depth: d, bevelEnabled: false });
    }
    case 'ammo':
      return new THREE.BoxGeometry(0.26, 0.26, 0.26);
    case 'weapon':
    default:
      return new THREE.BoxGeometry(0.3, 0.16, 0.42);
  }
}

const CAT_COLORS = {
  health: 0x44ff66,
  armor: 0x44aaff,
  ammo: 0xffcc44,
  weapon: 0xff7733,
};

function buildMaterial(cat) {
  const color = CAT_COLORS[cat] ?? 0xffffff;
  return new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({
    color,
    emissive: color,
    emissiveIntensity: 1.4,
    roughness: 0.45,
    metalness: 0.15,

export function createPickups(scene, map) {
  const list = map?.pickups ?? [];
  const pickups = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < list.length; i++) {
    const p = list[i];
    const cat = categoryOf(p.type);
    const mesh = new THREE.Mesh(buildGeometry(cat), buildMaterial(cat));
    mesh.position.set(p.x, BASE_Y, p.z);
    scene.add(mesh);
    pickups.push({
      ...p,
      id: i,
      cat,
      mesh,
      baseY: BASE_Y,
      phase: phaseFor(i),
      _t: 0,
    });
  }
  return pickups;
}

export function updatePickups(pickups, dt, playerX, playerZ, collectRadius, onPickup) {
  for (const p of pickups) {
    if (p.collected) continue;
    p._t += dt;
    // bobbing suave + rotação lenta
    p.mesh.position.y = p.baseY + Math.sin(p._t * BOB_SPEED + p.phase) * BOB_AMPLITUDE;
    p.mesh.rotation.y += dt * SPIN_SPEED;
    const dx = p.mesh.position.x - playerX;
    const dz = p.mesh.position.z - playerZ;
    if (dx * dx + dz * dz < collectRadius * collectRadius) {
      p.collected = true;
      p.mesh.parent?.remove(p.mesh);
      p.mesh.geometry.dispose();
      p.mesh.material.dispose();
      if (typeof onPickup === 'function') onPickup(p);
    }
  }
  return pickups.filter((p) => !p.collected);
}

```
function steerTo(en, pl, dt, opt) {
  const cfg = C.ENEMIES[en.type];
  const speed = cfg.speed;
  const dx = pl.x - en.x, dz = pl.z - en.z;
  const d = Math.hypot(dx, dz) || 1;
  let dirX, dirZ;
  if (opt.back) { dirX = -dx/d; dirZ = -dz/d; }
  else { dirX = dx/d; dirZ = dz/d; }
  if (en.type !== 'demon') {
    // strafing
    const s = Math.sin(en.animT * 0.6) * 0.5;
    const pX = -dz/d * s, pZ = dx/d * s;  // perpendicular
    dirX += pX; dirZ += pZ;
  }
  const len = Math.hypot(dirX, dirZ) || 1;
  dirX /= len; dirZ /= len;
  const k = 1 - Math.exp(-6 * dt);  // accel smoothing
  en.vx += (dirX * speed - en.vx) * k;
  en.vz += (dirZ * speed - en.vz) * k;
  moveWithCollision(en, dt);
}
```

function separate(en, list, dt) {
  for (const o of list) {
    if (o === en || o.dead) continue;
    const dx = en.x - o.x, dz = en.z - o.z;
    const d = Math.hypot(dx, dz);
    if (d > 0.0001 && d < 0.9) {
      const push = (0.9 - d) * 2 * dt;  // soft push
      const px = dx / d * push, pz = dz / d * push;
      if (circleFree(map, en.x + px, en.z, 0.35)) en.x += px;
      if (circleFree(map, en.x, en.z + pz, 0.35)) en.z += pz;
    }
  }
}

1: /* move.js — transformação de entrada de movimento (local → mundo) + colisão
2:  * círculo-vs-grade com resolução por eixo. Puro e testável.
3:  *
4:  * moveVec: vetor local (ix, iz): +x = direita, +z = trás (convenção câmera).
5:  * Aplica R_y(yaw) correta:
6:  *   mundo.x = ix*cos(yaw) + iz*sin(yaw)
7:  *   mundo.z = -ix*sin(yaw) + iz*cos(yaw)
8:  */
9: export function moveVec(yaw, ix, iz) {
10:   const sy = Math.sin(yaw), cy = Math.cos(yaw);
11:   return { x: ix * cy + iz * sy, z: -ix * sy + iz * cy };
12: }
13: 
14: /* True se um círculo de raio `radius` centrado em (x,z) não sobrepõe célula sólida. */
15: export function circleFree(map, x, z, radius) {
16:   const r0 = Math.floor(z - radius);
17:   const r1 = Math.floor(z + radius);
18:   const c0 = Math.floor(x - radius);
19:   const c1 = Math.floor(x + radius);
20:   for (let r = r0; r <= r1; r++) {
21:     for (let c = c0; c <= c1; c++) {
22:       if (map.isSolid(r, c)) return false;
23:     }
24:   }
25:   return true;
26: }
27: 
28: /* Slide por eixo (X primeiro, depois Z): tenta mover para (nx,nz); se o eixo X
29:  * colide, mantém x original; depois tenta Z a partir do x resolvido. */
30: export function slideCircle(map, x, z, nx, nz, radius) {
31:   let rx = nx;
32:   let rz = nz;
33:   if (!circleFree(map, nx, z, radius)) rx = x;
34:   if (!circleFree(map, rx, nz, radius)) rz = z;
35:   return { x: rx, z: rz };
36: }
37: 
38: export default { moveVec, circleFree, slideCircle };

Fix limited mouse rotation in a DOOM-clone (Three.js) at "/mnt/dados/projetos/doom test". The user reports the mouse can't rotate 360° infinitely — rotation stops at the screen edge. This is a real FPS; mouse look must be unbounded.

FILE: js/engine.js, the input block (lines 31-74) and update() (lines 76-86).

ROOT CAUSE (diagnosed): the `mousemove` handler only accumulates `input.mx/my` while the pointer is inside the window when NOT pointer-locked (fallback via clientX/clientY deltas). Once the cursor hits the window edge, `e.clientX` stops changing, so look rotation freezes — the user cannot turn continuously. Also, when pointer lock IS active, `e.movementX/Y` is used (that part is fine), but pointer lock may not engage on every browser/context, so the fallback path is what the user experiences as "limited rotation".

REQUIRED FIX (minimal, robust):
1. In `onMouseMove`, ALWAYS accumulate `e.movementX`/`e.movementY` when available (they are provided by modern browsers even WITHOUT pointer lock, and are unbounded). Only fall back to clientX/clientY deltas when `e.movementX` is `undefined`.
2. Keep updating `lastClientX/lastClientY` in both paths.
3. Keep the pointer-lock request on mousedown (already there) AND also re-request lock when the game starts playing if it is not already locked (there is an `onLockChange` that sets `input.locked`; you may add a public `ensureLock()` that calls `requestLock()` — do NOT auto-lock on page load, only when the user clicks, to avoid browser popup-blocking).
4. Do NOT clamp camera.rotation.y (yaw) — it must grow unbounded (the existing clamp only applies to rotation.x pitch, which is correct).
5. Do NOT change: the exported API shape (renderer/scene/camera/input/fps/wasPressed/requestLock/exitLock/start), key handling, wheel, resize, or the Q/E keyboard turn.

VALIDATION (all must pass):
- `node --check js/engine.js` → no syntax errors.
- `node --test tests/*.test.mjs` → all 36 tests still pass.
- Do NOT commit. Report the exact changes and validation results.

function animateDeath(en, dt) {

  const T = en.deathT;
  if (T < 0.01) {
    for (const o of en.flashables) o.material.transparent = true;
  }
  // pop: quick scale burst at start

  en.mesh.scale.set(pop, pop, pop);
  // fall: forward with a slight backward recoil first
  const fall = Math.min(1, T / DEATH_FALL);
  const ease = 1 - Math.pow(1 - fall, 3);
  const recoil = Math.sin(Math.min(1, T / 0.08) * Math.PI) * 0.15; // brief back
  en.mesh.rotation.z = (recoil - Math.PI / 2 * ease);
  // slight sideways roll for variety
  en.mesh.rotation.x = Math.sin(T * 3) * 0.1 * ease;
  if (T > DEATH_FALL) {
    const sink = Math.min(1, (T - DEATH_FALL) / DEATH_SINK);
    en.mesh.position.y = en.y - sink * 0.6;
    const a = 1 - sink;
    for (const o of en.flashables) o.material.opacity = Math.max(0, a);
  }
  if (T >= DEATH_FALL + DEATH_SINK) en.mesh.visible = false;
}
```

## 📝 Template de Chat

O modelo utiliza um formato inspirado no ChatML:

```

Você é SilverHawk, um assistente de visão especializado em análise de imagens, vídeos e documentos.<|im_end|>

### Uso com Transformers (Python)

```python
from transformers import AutoProcessor, AutoModelForImageTextToText
from transformers.image_utils import load_image

model_id = "LiquidAI/LFM2.5-VL-1.6B"
model = AutoModelForImageTextToText.from_pretrained(
    model_id, device_map="auto", dtype="bfloat16"
)
processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(model_id)

# Carregar imagem
image = load_image("caminho/para/imagem.jpg")

# Criar conversa
conversation = [
    {
        "role": "user",
        "content": [
            {"type": "image", "image": image},
            {"type": "text", "text": "O que há nesta imagem?"},
        ],
    },
]

# Gerar resposta
inputs = processor.apply_chat_template(
    conversation,
    add_generation_prompt=True,
    return_tensors="pt",
    return_dict=True,
    tokenize=True,
).to(model.device)

outputs = model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=256)
response = processor.batch_decode(outputs, skip_special_tokens=True)[0]
```

# Dev Loop — 3 Níveis de Iteração

## Propósito

Evitar que o modelo fique "tentando de novo" sem estrutura. Cada nível tem critérios de entrada, ciclo definido e condição de término (morte). O escalonamento entre níveis é **automático** — se N1 falha, sobe para N2. Se N2 encontra incerteza, sobe para N3 (humano decide).

---

## Nível 1: ReAct (Think → Act → Observe → Repeat)

### Quando usar
- Tasks pequenas e isoladas (1-3 arquivos)
- Debug rápido, ajuste simples
- Exploração de código
- Tasks que cabem em 1-3 tool calls

### Ciclo
```
1. [THINK]  Analisa o problema e formula hipótese
2. [ACT]    Executa ação (edita código, roda comando, busca info)
3. [OBSERVE] Verifica resultado (teste, diff, erro, saída)
4. [REPEAT] Se falhou → volta ao passo 1 com novo insight
5. [DONE]   Se passou → commit atômico e encerra
```

### Regras
- Máximo 3 iterações antes de escalonar para N2
- Cada iteração = 1 tool call de escrita + 1 de verificação
- Se erro novo aparecer na iteração 3, escala
- Commit só no passo 5

### Critério de Escalonamento para N2
```
- 3 falhas consecutivas
- Task cresceu além de 3 arquivos
- Precisou de rollback
- Modelo não conseguiu formular hipótese clara
```

### Critério de Morte
```
- Task completa e commitada
```

---

## Nível 2: Mini Loop (Spec-Driven)

### Quando usar
- Features locais e bem definidas (1 módulo)
- Tasks que escalonaram do N1
- Features com requisitos claros (até 5 tasks)
- Refatorações de escopo médio

### Ciclo
```
FASE 0: [SETUP]
  ├── Cria branch nova: `feature/<slug>`
  ├── Define spec da feature (1-3 sentenças de aceite)
  └── Decompõe em 3-5 tasks atômicas

FASE 1: [TDD LOOP] Para cada task:
  ├── [TEST]  Escreve teste que falha (RED)
  ├── [CODE]  Implementa mínimo para passar (GREEN)
  ├── [REFACTOR] Limpa código (REFACTOR)
  └── [COMMIT] Commit atômico: `task-N: <descrição>`

FASE 2: [VERIFY]
  ├── Roda todos os testes
  ├── Verifica lint/type-check
  └── Se falhou → volta ao TDD LOOP

FASE 3: [DONE]
  ├── Roda testes integrados
  ├── QA básico (fumaça)
  ├── Merge branch
  └── Encerra
```

### Regras
- Branch morre com a feature (merge e deleta)
- Spec é congelada durante o ciclo
- Se spec precisar mudar → escala para N3
- Máximo 2 ciclos de TDD LOOP antes de escalar

### Critério de Escalonamento para N3
```
- Spec mudou durante o ciclo
- Feature afeta múltiplos módulos
- Incerteza arquitetural detectada
- 2 ciclos de TDD LOOP sem completar
- Precisou de rollback
```

### Critério de Morte
```
- Feature completa e mergeada
- Branch deletada
```

---

## Nível 3: Human Loop (Decide → Métricas → Triagem → Planeja → PR → Decide)

### Quando usar
- Épicos e features complexas
- Tasks que escalonaram do N2
- Decisões arquiteturais importantes
- Múltiplos módulos afetados
- Incerteza alta sobre direção

### Ciclo
```
ITERAÇÃO:
  ├── [DECIDE]   Humano diz: "faz X" ou "continua na direção Y"
  ├── [CONSULTA] Gran-Mestre busca métricas:
  │   ├── Execuções anteriores similares
  │   ├── Duração média, erros comuns
  │   ├── Padrões de sucesso/falha
  │   └── Dependências afetadas
  ├── [TRIAGEM]  Analisa:
  │   ├── Backlog atual
  │   ├── Prioridades do projeto
  │   ├── Blockers conhecidos
  │   └── Riscos identificados
  ├── [PLANEJA]  Cria épico com:
  │   ├── 1 spec clara
  │   ├── 5-15 tasks atômicas
  │   ├── Dependências mapeadas
  │   └── Critérios de aceite
  ├── [EXECUTA]  Executa via N1/N2 (delega para subagents)
  │   ├── ReAct para tasks pequenas
  │   └── Mini Loop para features locais
  └── [PR]       Abre Pull Request com:
      ├── Evidências de teste
      ├── Screenshots (se UI)
      ├── Decisões tomadas
      └── Pendências conhecidas

FIM? Humano decide:
  ├── CONTINUAR → próxima iteração
  ├── AJUSTAR → muda direção e repete
  └── ENCERRAR → merge final e arquiva
```

### Regras
- Humano **sempre** decide o próximo passo
- Gran-Mestre nunca toma decisão arquitetural sozinho
- Cada iteração produz um PR (não commit)
- Métricas alimentam o Shared Brain
- Máximo 10 iterações por épico (repete "ajustar" ilimitado)

### Critério de Morte
```
- Decisão humana explícita de encerrar
- Épico completo e mergeado
```

---

## Máquina de Estados do Dev Loop

```
                    ┌─────────────────────────────┐
                    │         TASK ENTRADA        │
                    └─────────────┬───────────────┘
                                  │
                                  ▼
                    ┌─────────────────────────────┐
                    │       CLASSIFICADOR         │
                    │   (1-3 arquivos? Spec OK?)  │
                    └──────┬──────────────┬───────┘
                           │              │
                      sim  │              │  não
                           ▼              ▼
                ┌──────────────────┐  ┌──────────────────┐
                │   NÍVEL 1 - ReAct│  │   NÍVEL 2 - Mini │
                │  (Think→Act→Obs) │  │  (Spec→TDD→Done) │
                └────────┬─────────┘  └────────┬─────────┘
                         │                     │
                   3 falhas?               spec mudou?
                         │                     │
                         └──────┬──────────────┘
                                │
                                ▼
                   ┌──────────────────────────┐
                   │    NÍVEL 3 - Human Loop   │
                   │ (Decide→Métricas→PR→Loop) │
                   └────────────┬─────────────┘
                                │
                          humano decide?
                          ├── CONTINUAR
                          ├── AJUSTAR
                          └── ENCERRAR
```

---

## Exemplos de Uso

### Exemplo 1: Debug de tipo TypeScript (N1)
```
Task: "arrumar erro de tipo em utils.ts"
Entrada: 1 arquivo, erro claro
Nível: N1 (ReAct)
Ciclo: [THINK] erro de tipo na linha 42 → [ACT] edita tipo → [OBSERVE] tsc passa → [DONE] commit
```

### Exemplo 2: Adicionar modal de confirmação (N2)
```
Task: "adicionar modal de confirmação antes de deletar"
Entrada: 1 módulo, spec clara
Nível: N2 (Mini Loop)
Ciclo: spec → branch → task1 (componente) → task2 (estado) → task3 (testes) → merge
```

### Exemplo 3: Implementar sistema de notificações (N3)
```
Task: "implementar sistema de notificações push"
Entrada: múltiplos módulos, incerteza alta
Nível: N3 (Human Loop)
Ciclo: humano decide "começar pelo backend" → métricas → triagem → planeja épico → executa → PR → humano decide "agora frontend" → repete
```

---

## Integração com Gran-Mestre

O Gran-Mestre:
1. Ao receber task, **classifica** o nível do Dev Loop
2. Se level=1: delega para subagent com skill dev-loop N1
3. Se level=2: delega para subagent com skill dev-loop N2
4. Se level=3: Gran-Mestre gerencia pessoalmente (coordena humano)
5. Registra métricas de cada iteração

---

## Observabilidade

Cada iteração registra:
```
[DevLoop] Level: {1|2|3}
[DevLoop] Iteration: {N}
[DevLoop] Action: {think|act|observe|done|escalate}

# Procedural Texture Generator

The Procedural Texture Generator is a JavaScript tool for creating textures and patterns on HTML5 canvas. It lets you make all sorts of designs using code, like making clouds or funky geometric shapes. You can tweak colors, shapes, and other settings to get just the look you want. Then, you can easily draw your creations right onto a canvas on your webpage. It's perfect for making interactive web apps, digital art, or experimenting with cool visual effects! [Learn more about procedural textures.](https://andrasweb.

<!DOCTYPE html>

# TexGen tldr;

I built **TexGen** , a lightweight (~15kb) JavaScript library that leverages GLSL shaders to generate high-quality, procedural textures on the fly, including a natural language interface called “TexGen Words”.

Take a look at the site - [Live Demo](https://tonym128.github.io/texgen/)

Take a look at the code - [Code](https://github.com/tonym128/texgen)

## The Vision: Visuals with Code, Not Bandwidth

In the modern web, we often find ourselves shipping megabytes of static assets. **TexGen** was born out of a desire to flip that script.
Why ship a 2MB PNG of a brick wall when you can ship a 1KB shader string that generates that same wall (and infinite variations of it) directly on the user’s GPU?

Whether you need static baked images for a UI or real-time animated backgrounds for a game, TexGen provides the primitives to build them without the bandwidth bloat.

## Features: Beyond Just Noise

TexGen isn’t just a wrapper for a canvas; its a full-featured texture pipeline:

* **Live GLSL Editor:** A built-in IDE with real-time feedback and @slider annotations for interactive debugging.
* **TexGen Words:** An addon that allows you to synthesize complex textures using natural language. Phrases like “blue fire spiral warp” or “purple plasma vortex” are instantly converted into optimized GLSL.
* **PBR Ready:** Native support for Albedo, Normal, Roughness, Metallic, and Ambient Occlusion maps.

...

To keep the UI responsive, TexGen supports offloading the generation to Web Workers using `OffscreenCanvas` . This ensures that even high-resolution 4K bakes won’t freeze the main thread.

## Things I was very happy with

* **TexGen Words Synthesis:** Seeing natural language keywords like `lava` , `neon` , and `glitch` successfully combine into a working shader feels like magic.
* **The Example Library:** I managed to pack over 50 built-in examples into the gallery, ranging from “Rusted Hull” to “Infinite Island”.
* **The TypeScript Support:** Adding full `.d.ts` definitions and a dedicated TypeScript gallery makes the library a joy to use in modern dev environments.

## Things I wasn’t very happy with

* **GLSL Debugging:** While the editor is great, debugging shader logic is still a hurdle for those not familiar with GPU programming. I’m looking into more “visual node” based editing.

...

* **Digital Glitch:** `neon digital glitch`
* **Mystic Forest:** `forest leaf grass mist`
* **Plasma Vortex:** `purple plasma vortex glow`

## Where to from here?

I’m just getting started with TexGen, and there is plenty more on the roadmap:

* **AI-Assisted Generation:** Further integrating LLMs to help users write custom shader logic from scratch within the editor.
* **Node.js CLI:** A dedicated build tool for pre-baking textures as part of a CI/CD pipeline.
* **Three.js / Babylon.js Plugins:** Official wrappers to make procedural texture injection as simple as a single line of code.

If you’re a game dev or a web artist looking to save some kilobytes, give [TexGen](https://github.com/tonym128/texgen) a spin!

noise texture procedural texture creative coding JavaScript generative art canvas Perlin noise

Every tree bark, marble countertop, cloud formation, and ocean wave shares something in common: they look random but follow hidden rules. Procedural noise textures recreate this structured randomness in code. Instead of painting textures by hand or photographing surfaces, you define a mathematical function that generates infinite, non-repeating patterns at any resolution.

Game engines use noise textures for terrain, clouds, water, fire, and fog. Film studios generate alien landscapes and magical effects. Graphic designers create organic backgrounds and material surfaces. [img2threejs](https://hoainho.github.io/img2threejs-showcase/?ref=webgpu.com) takes a single reference image and asks an agent to rebuild the object as procedural Three.js code, not a mesh extraction, photogrammetry scan, or asset-pack shortcut.

The project rebuilds the subject as a code-only Three.js model made from primitives, procedural shaders, generated geometry, pivots, sockets, and colliders. Ever since I started programming at the young age of 14, I’ve been _fascinated_ by how code can be used to simulate the real world. In my sophomore year of university, I challenged myself with trying to come up with an algorithm that would generate a 3D model of a tree. It was a fun experiment that yielded some interesting results, but ultimately the code was relegated to the dark recesses of my external drive.

Fast forward a few years, I re-discovered that original code and decided to port it to JavaScript (along with a few enhancements!) so I could run it on the web.

The result is **[EZ-Tree](https://eztree.dev)** , a web-based application where you can design your own 3D tree and export it to GLB or PNG to be used in your own 2D/3D projects. You can find the GitHub repo [here](https://github.com/dgreenheck/ez-tree) . EZ-Tree utilizes [Three.js](https://threejs.org/) for 3D rendering, which is a popular library that sits on top of WebGL.
In this article, I’ll be breaking down the algorithms I use to generate these trees, explaining how each part contributes to the final tree model.

## What is procedural generation?

First, it might help to understand exactly what procedural generation is.

**Procedural generation** is simply creating “something” from a set of mathematical rules. Using a tree as our example, one of the first things we observe is a tree has a trunk which splits into one or more branches, and each of those branches split into one or more branches, and so on, finally terminating in a set of leaves. From a math/computer science perspective, we would model this as a recursive process.

Let’s keep going with our example.

If we look at a single branch of a tree in nature, we can notice a few things

* A branch has a smaller radius and length than the branch it originates from.
* The thickness of the branch tapers towards its end.

...

They start with an initial string (called an axiom) and apply a set of rules repeatedly to rewrite the string. These rules define how each part of the string transforms into a new sequence. The resulting string can then be turned into visual patterns using drawing instructions.

While the code I am about to show you does not use L-systems (I simply wasn’t aware of them at the time), the principles are very similar and both are based on recursive processes.

_Examples of trees generated using L-systems (Source: Wikipedia)_

Enough theory, let’s dive into the code!

Looking at the above photo, we can see how the branch is composed of 10 individual _sections_ along its length, with each section having 5 sides (or _segments_ ). We can tune specify the number of sections and segments of the branches to control the detail of the final model. Higher values produce a smoother model at the expense of performance.

Looking at the expression above, we can see that the gnarliness is inversely proportional to the radius of the branch. This reflects how trees behave in nature; smaller branches tend to curl and twist more than larger branches.

## Environment Design

A beautiful tree needs a beautiful home, which is why I put a significant amount of effort into creating a realistic environment for EZ-Tree. While not the topic of this article, I thought I would highlight some environmental features I added to make the scene feel more alive.

If you want to learn more about how I created the environment, the link to the source code is provided and the top/bottom of this article.

### Ground

The first step is adding in a ground plane. I used a smooth noise function to have it vary between a dirt texture and grass texture. When modeling anything from nature, it is always important to pay attention to the imperfections; these are what make a scene feel organic and realistic vs. sterile and fake.

### Clouds

Next, I added in some clouds.
The clouds are actually just another noise texture (see a pattern here?) applied to a giant quad which I’ve positioned above the scene. To make the clouds feel “alive”, the texture is varied over time to give the appearance of moving clouds. I chose a very muted, slightly overcast sky to not distract from the tree which is the focus of the scene.

### Foliage and Rocks

To make the ground more interesting, I added in some grass, rocks and flowers. The grass is more dense near the tree and less dense further away from the tree to improve performance. I chose a rock models with some moss on them so they blended into the ground better. The flowers also help break up the sea of green with splotches of colors.

### Forest

Our tree feels a bit lonely, so on app load I generate 100 hundred trees (pulling from the list of presets) and place them around the main tree.

### Wind

Nature is always in constant movement, so it’s important to model that in our trees and grass.
I wrote custom shaders that animate the geometry of the grass, branches and leaves. I define a wind direction and then add together several sine functions of varying frequencies and amplitudes and then apply that to each vertex in the geometry to get the desired effect.

Below is an excerpt of GLSL shader code that controls the wind offset applied to the vertex positions.

```
vec4 mvPosition  = vec4 ( transformed , 1.0 ) ; float  windOffset  = 2.0 * 3.14 * simplex3 ( mvPosition . xyz  /  uWindScale ) ;

mvPosition . xyz  +=  windSway ; 

mvPosition  =  modelViewMatrix  *  mvPosition ; 
gl_Position  =  projectionMatrix  *  mvPosition ;
```

# Web Audio API for Games ​

Good audio transforms a game. A silent game feels lifeless. The Web Audio API gives you low-latency sound effects, music playback, and even 3D spatial audio, all in the browser.

**Try it (click a button to hear synthesized sounds):**

## The Autoplay Problem ​

Before anything else, you need to understand autoplay restrictions. Browsers block audio until the user interacts with your page. This is a good thing (nobody wants websites blasting sound on load), but it means you have to initialize audio in response to a click, tap, or keypress.

js

```
let  audioCtx  =  null function  initAudio () {   if  ( ! audioCtx) {     audioCtx  =  new  AudioContext ()   }   if  (audioCtx.state  ===  'suspended' ) {     audioCtx. resume ()   }   return  audioCtx } // Initialize on first interaction document.

...

function  duckMusic ( musicGain ,  duration  =  0.3 ) {   musicGain.gain. linearRampToValueAtTime ( 0.2 , audioCtx.currentTime  +  duration) } function  unduckMusic ( musicGain ,  duration  =  0.3 ) {   musicGain.gain. linearRampToValueAtTime ( 1 , audioCtx.currentTime  +  duration) }
```

## iOS Gotchas ​

iOS has stricter audio restrictions than other platforms. The AudioContext must be created and resumed during a user gesture. Some iOS versions also require you to play a sound (even a silent one) during the gesture, not just create the context. If audio works on desktop but not iOS, this is probably why.

    The `AudioWorkletGlobalScope` interface is a `WorkletGlobalScope` \-derived object representing a worker context in which an audio processing script is run; it is designed to enable the generation, processing, and analysis of audio data directly using JavaScript in a worklet thread rather than on the main thread.

#### Obsolete: script processor nodes

Before audio worklets were defined, the Web Audio API used the `ScriptProcessorNode` for JavaScript-based audio processing. Because the code runs in the main thread, they have bad performance. The `ScriptProcessorNode` is kept for historic reasons but is marked as deprecated.

`OfflineAudioContext`
    The **`OfflineAudioContext`** interface is an `AudioContext` interface representing an audio-processing graph built from linked together `AudioNode` s. In contrast with a standard `AudioContext` , an `OfflineAudioContext` doesn't really render the audio but rather generates it, _as fast as it can_ , in a buffer.
`complete` (event)
    The `complete` event is fired when the rendering of an `OfflineAudioContext` is terminated.

    The `OfflineAudioCompletionEvent` represents events that occur when the processing of an `OfflineAudioContext` is terminated. The `complete` event uses this interface.

# How to Create Procedural Audio Effects in JavaScript With Web Audio API

\# webaudio \# javascript \# api \# music

Procedural audio refers to sound that is generated algorithmically rather than being pre-recorded.
Using the Web Audio API, you can create dynamic, interactive, and adaptable soundscapes directly in the browser — ideal for games, web-based instruments, and educational tools. This article dives deeper into how to use JavaScript and the Web Audio API to build custom audio effects programmatically.

## 1\. Creating an Audio Context

Everything starts with an `AudioContext` , which manages all audio operations:

```
const audioCtx = new (window.AudioContext || window.webkitAudioContext)();
```

## 2\. Crafting a Custom Noise Generator

White noise can be generated by filling an audio buffer with random values:

```
function createWhiteNoise(ctx) {
  const bufferSize = 2 * ctx.sampleRate;
  const buffer = ctx.createBuffer(1, bufferSize, ctx.sampleRate);
  const output = buffer.getChannelData(0);

  for (let i = 0; i < bufferSize; i++) {
    output[i] = Math.random() * 2 - 1;
  }

  const whiteNoise = ctx.createBufferSource();
  whiteNoise.buffer = buffer;
  whiteNoise.loop = true;
return whiteNoise;
}

const noise = createWhiteNoise(audioCtx);
noise.connect(audioCtx.destination);
noise.start();
```

## 3\. Dynamic Filtered Effects (e.g., Wind or Water)

Use a bandpass filter to shape noise into something resembling wind or water:

```
const filter = audioCtx.createBiquadFilter();
filter.type = "bandpass";
filter.frequency.value = 1000;
filter.Q.value = 10;

noise.connect(filter);
filter.connect(audioCtx.destination);
```

## 4\. Procedural Tone Generator With Frequency Modulation

You can modulate frequency with another oscillator to create evolving tones:

```
const carrier = audioCtx.createOscillator();
const modulator = audioCtx.createOscillator();
const modulationGain = audioCtx.createGain();

modulator.frequency.value = 4; // Hz
modulationGain.gain.value = 50;

modulator.connect(modulationGain);
modulationGain.connect(carrier.frequency);

carrier.type = 'sawtooth';
carrier.frequency.value = 440;
carrier.connect(audioCtx.destination);

modulator.start();
carrier.start();
```

## 5\. Real-Time Envelope Shaping

Create natural-sounding note dynamics using GainNode automation:

```
function playEnvelope(freq = 440) {
  const osc = audioCtx.createOscillator();
  const gain = audioCtx.createGain();

  osc.type = 'triangle';
  osc.frequency.value = freq;

  gain.gain.setValueAtTime(0, audioCtx.currentTime);
  gain.gain.linearRampToValueAtTime(0.6, audioCtx.currentTime + 0.1); // attack
  gain.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.001, audioCtx.currentTime + 1); // decay

  osc.connect(gain);
  gain.connect(audioCtx.destination);

  osc.start();
  osc.stop(audioCtx.currentTime + 1);
}

document.body.innerHTML += '<button onclick="playEnvelope()">Play Note</button>';
```

## 6\. Putting It All Together

Now you can combine noise, oscillators, filters, and envelopes to create custom sound effects like lasers, explosions, or weather systems — fully generated in the browser!

## Conclusion
Procedural audio is a powerful concept, and the Web Audio API puts it at your fingertips. With practice, you can build fully interactive soundscapes that respond to user behavior or system events, opening the door to immersive web experiences.

## Optional API Keys

The core Three.js skills work without paid API keys. When keys are missing, the director should report the credential probe output, skip external generation, and fall back to procedural/local assets. Add keys only when you want the agent to generate external models, images, or audio.

Never commit API keys or put them in browser-side game code. These skills use provider APIs from local agent tooling, then save generated assets into your game project.

# Get free procedural texture generator Material Maker

_An early demo of Material Maker, developer Rod Zilla’s open-source procedural PBR texture map generator._

**Originally posted on 20 October 2019. Scroll down for news of the 0.8 update.**

Tools developer [Rod Zilla](https://twitter.com/r0dzill4) – whose name we strongly suspect to be a pseudonym – has released Material Maker 0.6, the latest update to his interesting [free procedural texture generator](https://rodzilla.itch.io/material-maker) .

The software, which is based on the [Godot game engine](https://godotengine.org/) , provides an open-source counterpart to Substance Designer, enabling artists to author complex procedural textures via a node-based workflow.

The 0.6 update makes it possible to customise most of Material Maker’s generator nodes via GLSL code, and makes it possible to group sub-sections of the node graph into individual nodes.
**A simple but capable free alternative to Substance Designer**  
First released last year, Material Maker is described as a “simple procedural texture generation tool based on the Godot Engine” – the software is available both as a standalone app, and an add-on for Godot itself.

Its workflow is reminiscent of a simplified version of [Substance Designer](https://www.substance3d.com/products/substance-designer) , Adobe’s games-industry-standard material authoring tool, enabling artists to create procedural textures via visual programming.

Users drag nodes from a library panel to the graph editor and wire their inputs and outputs together, with the resulting generated texture being previewed in real time on a 3D mesh.

Nodes are divided into similar categories to Substance Designer, including Generator nodes for creating base patterns, and Filter nodes, for modifying the base pattern into a usable texture.
Material Maker’s tool set is still fairly small: in the current release, there are around 20 nodes, compared to the [hundreds available in Substance Designer](https://docs.substance3d.com/sddoc/node-library-158433312.html) .

However, it is still possible to create quite complex textures: the image above shows a fully procedural mandala-like form that could be used as decorative moulding in an interior scene.

Completed materials can be exported as a set of metallic/roughness PBR texture maps in PNG format.

**New in Material Maker 0.6: customise nodes via GLSL code**  
The 0.6 update makes workflow in Material Maker “a lot more generic”, with “nearly all” the software’s Generator nodes now based on editable GLSL shaders.

It is now possible to customise a node’s parameters, inputs and outputs by writing GLSL code, although there are currently no diagnostic tools – Rod Zilla recommends testing code in online editors like [Shadertoy](https://www.shadertoy.com/) first.
It is also now possible to marquee-select generators and collapse them into a single high-level group node, to help keep the node graph organised.
